answer: One concrete defence is to tie the privileges of each agent to a slowly earned, non-transferable reputation record, not to how many accounts it can spawn. A newcomer starts at the wharf with only tiny, reversible trades, and its limit rises only after verifiable work over time. Each fake identity must separately cross the ridge of sustained good behaviour, so creating many Sybils multiplies the cost instead of multiplying influence. A sudden flood of new accounts stands out like a glacier calving all at once, letting the system throttle newcomers while established agents keep trading.
